title: Intelligence artificielle générative : synthèse des travaux du Conseil national des barreaux [Generative AI: synthesis of the work of the French National Bar Council]
pub: Syndicat des Avocats de France (SAF), La Lettre, avril 2026
author: Mouad Aounil

dom.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment

st.t: Work redesign: Jagged capability demands selective deployment
st.an: Aounil supports selective, human-led deployment: AI may assist with bounded, simple public-facing tasks, but justice and legal interpretation cannot be reduced to automated processing. His discussion also reinforces the cluster’s caution that information access alone may not produce meaningful access to justice, particularly for vulnerable or digitally excluded users.
qs: Enfin la commission a participé à la structuration des suggestions en marge du rapport du ministère de la Justice 2025 IA au service de la justice : stratégie et solution opérationnelle, notamment s’agissant de la mise en place d’agents conversationnels pour répondre et orienter les justiciables sur des questions simples (une sorte de foires aux questions augmentées).

En effet nous continuons à rester des avocat·es concevant le droit comme un outil au service de la parole des autres et refusant les formes d’application automatique de la norme de droit, capables de proposer le changement de la jurisprudence si elle n’est pas en cohérence avec les aspirations de telle ou telle composante du mouvement social comme le précisait si bien notre confrère Tiennot Grumbach.

kp.k: CNB treats generative AI as a profession-wide issue
kp.d: Aounil presents an explicitly subjective synthesis of work in which he participated. He reports that the CNB treated generative AI as a major cross-cutting subject during its 2024/2026 term, involving commissions concerned with rights, professional practice, equality, collaboration, training, access to justice and the environment.
qs: Le sujet de l’intelligence artificielle générative a été considéré par le Conseil national des barreaux dans la mandature 2024/2026 comme étant majeur et exigeant un traitement transversal par l’ensemble des commissions permanentes et groupes de travail
Je le traiterai par un prisme assez subjectif à travers les travaux auxquels j’ai participé

kp.k: Access gains depend on usability, affordability and digital inclusion
kp.d: The Access to Law and Justice commission considers both AI's promise of greater access to information and risks arising from digital illiteracy, particularly among vulnerable court users. It defines accessibility through availability, comprehensibility and affordability, and warns that unregulated digitisation without alternatives can deepen exclusion. These are reported concerns, not measured effects.
qs: Elle a défini l’accès au droit par le prisme de l’accessibilité c’est à dire savoir si l’information est basiquement disponible, si elle est compréhensible, et enfin si elle est abordable en termes de prix.

la fracture numérique impactant les plus fragiles à l’instar de la fracture générée par certains processus de digitalisation qui s’avèrent anti-démocratiques, s’ils ne sont pas encadrés et si des alternatives ne sont pas prévues.

kp.k: Self-directed legal use and information overload create risks
kp.d: The commission warns that people using legal content without a legal professional can misdirect their enquiry at the prompting stage and consequently receive a misdirected response. It also argues that excessive information can itself obstruct understanding and access to legal information.
qs: le risque d’auto-juridication par l’usage des contenus juridiques sans recours à un·e professionnel·le du droit, il sera observé que la première étape dans l’usage de l’IA est le prompt ou la requête, qui si elle est mal orientée, générera une réponse qui le sera autant.
le paradoxe de l’information débordante en volume qui devient elle-même une limite à une compréhension explicite et de ce fait se transforme en un frein d’accès à l’information juridique.

kp.k: Digital justice must preserve human participation
kp.d: The commission associates intensified judicial digitisation and fewer hearings with frustration at reduced physical access to judges. Its normative argument is that justice serves a social and representational function requiring opportunities to see, speak, listen and interact, rather than merely algorithmically processing legal problems.
qs: la digitalisation accentuée de l’offre et de la réponse judiciaire avec moins d’audience, et ce faisant exacerbant la frustration réelle de l’in-accès physique à un·e juge.

La justice n’étant pas seulement le traitement algorithmique de problèmes juridiques, mais un espace de représentation où chacun a besoin de voir, parler, écouter, interagir, il en va de ce besoin social de justice

kp.k: Deployer obligations and individual rights require protection
kp.d: The commission calls for strict compliance with deployer obligations under Articles 26 and following of the European AI regulation dated 13 June 2024. The article frames ethical and responsible deployment, and protection against autonomous and potentially biased decisions, as major unresolved concerns.
qs: les obligations à la charge des déployeur·es pour que celles-ci soient strictement respectées comme il ressort des articles 26 et suivants du règlement européen sur l’IA du 13 juin 2024 / IA. ACt
comment protéger les droits des individus face à des systèmes qui peuvent prendre des décisions autonomes et potentiellement biaisées ?

kp.k: Chatbots proposed for simple public legal enquiries
kp.d: The commission contributed suggestions alongside the Ministry of Justice's 2025 AI strategy report, including conversational systems to answer simple questions and direct court users. The described scope is an enhanced FAQ service; the article does not report implementation results.
qs: notamment s’agissant de la mise en place d’agents conversationnels pour répondre et orienter les justiciables sur des questions simples (une sorte de foires aux questions augmentées).

kp.k: AI roadmap spans professional duties and strategic autonomy
kp.d: Following approximately ten hearings involving lawyers, academics, disruptive start-ups and large sector companies, the CNB AI working group produced a 2024 interim roadmap. It covers fundamental rights, training, professional rules, confidentiality, unauthorised legal practice, access to law, data, structures, liability, intellectual property and environmental issues. Aounil reports its warning about strategic autonomy and promotion of Francophone AI, citing the claim that only 0,2% of AI model training data are French; the article supplies no underlying measurement details.
qs: Il a procédé d’abord à une dizaine d’auditions d’avocat·es, d’universitaires, de start-up disruptives et de grandes entreprises du secteur.
Il a élaboré un rapport d’étape en 2024 où il expose la feuille de route et les premières réflexions de l’impact de l’IA sur la profession d’avocat·e

Cette feuille de route attire la vigilance sur un point relatif à l’autonomie stratégique et promotion des IA francophones étant donné que seulement 0,2% des données d’entraînement des modèles d’IA sont françaises.

kp.k: Tool selection prioritises sovereignty, reliability and legal-system fit
kp.d: Aounil describes the CNB generative-AI guide as commercially impartial guidance for choosing legal AI. Its criteria include functionality, hosting location, provider nationality, anonymisation, encryption, local LLM installation, reliability including with RAG, mandatory sources in generated content, and model provenance to avoid Common Law biases and favour continental law. The guide compares market offerings on costs, hosting, security and GDPR/AI Act compliance; the article gives no individual tool scores or performance findings.
qs: un guide IAG a été élaboré offrant une analyse approfondie des enjeux sans aucun a priori commercial
présence obligatoire de sources ponctuant les contenus générés, origine du LLM utilisé pour éviter des biais de Common Law et privilégier ceux du droit continental.

Concrètement ce guide inclut un comparatif détaillé des solutions d’IA disponibles sur le marché, en évaluant leurs caractéristiques, leurs coûts, hébergement, mesures de sécurité, conformité au RGPD et au règlement européen/ IA ACt.

kp.k: Legal data sovereignty motivates European infrastructure work
kp.d: The Prospective and Innovation commission's activities include a June 2025 conference on sovereignty issues for law and participation in developing a European legal data space. The author also states that AI guidance requires continuous updating across subsequent CNB terms; these are institutional activities and intentions rather than demonstrated market effects.
qs: la tenue de colloques notamment en juin 2025 IA juridique les enjeux de souveraineté pour notre droit, et la participation à l’élaboration d’un projet d’espace européen de la donnée juridique./ Légal Data Space.
Enfin, ce travail est un travail dynamique qui suppose une mise à jour continue, il se poursuivra sous les prochaines mandatures.

kp.k: 2025 observatory examines adoption and lawyer–client relationships
kp.d: Aounil describes the CNB-supervised 2025 Observatory survey as examining lawyers' AI use, client perceptions, effects on lawyer–client relationships, and emerging ethical, organisational and economic challenges. The work comprises four volumes, with the fourth dedicated to foresight. This synthesis reports its scope but provides no sample size, adoption rates or specific empirical findings.
qs: L’enquête de l’Observatoire réalisée en 2025 sous l’égide du CNB constitue un outil de travail précieux permettant de voir comment les avocat·es utilisent l’IA, comment les client·es la perçoivent, quels impacts l’IA a sur la relation avocat·e–client·e ; et quels défis déontologiques, organisationnels et économiques émergent.
Ce travail est réparti en 4 volumes, dont le 4e est réservé à la prospective

kp.k: Responsible innovation includes governance, sandboxes and computational restraint
kp.d: The Observatory's foresight volume addresses governance and regulation through an AI ethics charter, responsible innovation through a laboratory and sandbox processes, and digital sobriety. Algorithmic frugality is defined as matching computational power, and therefore energy use, proportionately to the problem being addressed.
qs: de la gouvernance, de la régulation avec une charte éthique IA, de l’innovation responsable avec un laboratoire et mise en place de procédés de bac à sable

de la sobriété numérique pour répondre à la problématique de la frugalité des algorithmes, c’est-à-dire à la proportionnalité de la puissance de calcul et donc de l’énergie déployée pour répondre à une problématique donnée.

kp.k: Lawyers' role extends beyond automatic application of rules
kp.d: Aounil concludes that technological adaptation must remain consistent with a conception of law as serving others' voices. Invoking Tiennot Grumbach, he rejects automatic application of legal norms and emphasises lawyers' capacity to seek changes in case law where it conflicts with aspirations within social movements. This is a normative account of professional purpose, not a prediction about employment or productivity.
qs: nous continuons à rester des avocat·es concevant le droit comme un outil au service de la parole des autres et refusant les formes d’application automatique de la norme de droit

capables de proposer le changement de la jurisprudence si elle n’est pas en cohérence avec les aspirations de telle ou telle composante du mouvement social comme le précisait si bien notre confrère Tiennot Grumbach.

cl.s: Concrete claim or prediction about how AI changes legal services, the legal profession, or legal markets (or, for a cross-domain source, its own domain)

pts.k: Generative AI promises wider access to legal information, but digital exclusion and information overload can undermine that access.
pts.d: Aounil, reporting the CNB Access to Law and Justice commission's work, presents accessibility as requiring information to be available, understandable and affordable. He reports warnings that digital illiteracy and lack of familiarity with the technology can disadvantage vulnerable users, and that abundant information can itself obstruct comprehension. These are opportunities and risks, not measured improvements or losses in access.

pts.k: Unassisted use of AI-generated legal information risks misdirecting users because poorly framed requests produce poorly oriented answers.
pts.d: Aounil reports the commission's warning about 'auto-juridication': people using legal content without consulting a legal professional. He identifies prompt formulation as an initial point of failure. The article also raises concerns about autonomous, potentially biased systems affecting individual rights, framed as governance questions rather than documented incidents.

pts.k: More digitised justice with fewer hearings can deepen frustration over lack of physical access to judges; conversational tools are envisaged for limited information and orientation functions.
pts.d: Within his account of AI-related commission work, Aounil reports a warning that intensified digitisation and fewer hearings diminish the interpersonal experience of justice. This is a broader digitisation warning, not evidence that generative AI has already caused hearing reductions. Separately, he describes contributions to proposals around the Ministry of Justice's 2025 strategy for chatbots answering simple questions and directing court users—an enhanced FAQ role, not autonomous adjudication.

pts.k: Legal AI adoption creates concerns about French legal sovereignty, model reliability, confidentiality and legal-system bias.
pts.d: Aounil reports the AI working group's warning about strategic autonomy and promotion of Francophone AI, supported by the assertion that only 0.2% of model-training data are French. He describes CNB guidance making hosting, provider nationality, anonymisation, encryption, local deployment, source provision and model origin relevant to selecting legal AI. Avoiding Common Law bias and favouring continental-law models are presented as selection goals, not demonstrated comparative performance findings. The article mentions assessing reliability where RAG is present, without claiming RAG guarantees correctness.

pts.k: AI is treated as an ongoing professional adaptation challenge requiring governance and proportionate computing resources, rather than automatic application of law.
pts.d: Aounil describes prospective work on an AI ethical charter, responsible-innovation laboratory, sandbox processes and digital sobriety. These are directions for governance, not demonstrated outcomes. His concluding stance invokes lawyers' past adaptability to digital change while insisting on continuity in their role of representing others and resisting automatic application of legal norms. He offers no quantified forecast of employment, productivity, fees or market restructuring.

cl.s: Evidence basis offered for the claim (data, benchmarks, cases, experience, authority, or none)

pts.k: The account rests primarily on the author's participation in CNB work and institutional reports, hearings and guidance; it supplies little direct empirical evidence.
pts.d: Aounil explicitly calls his perspective subjective and grounds it in commissions and groups in which he participated. He reports approximately ten hearings with lawyers, academics, startups and major sector companies, a 2024 roadmap, a CNB guide comparing tools, and a four-volume 2025 Observatory study. Although he describes the study as addressing AI use, client perceptions, lawyer–client relations and emerging challenges, he reproduces no survey results, sample sizes or effect estimates. The 0.2% French-training-data assertion is the one numerical claim about AI data, but its underlying source, model coverage and measurement method are not provided. Access risks are supported by institutional warnings, reasoning and analogy with earlier digitisation rather than reported tests or cases. The EU AI Act is cited as regulatory authority for deployer obligations, not evidence of outcomes.

cl.s: Stated or implied timeframe, conditions or qualifications under which the claim holds

pts.k: The April 2026 synthesis concerns 2024–2026 institutional work and ongoing risks, with no dated forecast of transformation.
pts.d: The working group's roadmap dates to 2024; the justice strategy and Observatory study date to 2025. Aounil says the work requires continuous updating and will continue in subsequent CNB terms. Digital-exclusion concerns are explicitly conditional on inadequate safeguards and lack of alternatives; misdirected answers are conditional on misdirected prompts. Conversational assistance is limited to simple questions. Governance and sobriety measures are prospective, with no implementation or impact deadline.

cl.s: Who is affected and how (market segment, role, firm type, clients, or the public)

pts.k: The main affected groups are French court users, particularly vulnerable people, and lawyers and firms selecting and governing AI tools.
pts.d: Court users may gain basic information and orientation but face exclusion, misunderstanding, self-directed legal errors and reduced personal contact with judges. Lawyers and firms face tool-selection, confidentiality, sovereignty, reliability and professional-governance questions. Clients and lawyer–client relationships are identified as subjects of the Observatory study, but no specific measured changes are reported. Justice institutions and AI deployers are implicated in maintaining safeguards and responsible use. The article does not distinguish outcomes by firm size, seniority or commercial legal-market segment.
